title: Unified Inference: Q4 2026 Product Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Ava Martinez
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap and themes for Unified Inference (Q4 2026), updated pricing and packaging guidance, and the release notes for the 2026-11 feature rollout. It is the single-source reference for GTM, engineering, and support for this release.
product_overview:
Overview:
- Product: Unified Inference is Redwood's unified runtime and control plane for running LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Scope for Q4 2026: Stabilize model routing policies, rollout Redwood Optimize v6 integration, introduce per-route burst capacity controls for Dedicated, and update pricing to support tiered reserved capacity and compute-aware hosted rates.
- Core user problems addressed: unpredictable token cost, inconsistent latency across regions, difficulty rolling out model variants safely, and lack of production-grade observability for burst and tail latency.
Key capabilities delivered in this release:
1) Model routing cost-aware fallbacks with policy DSL and a UI for configuring cost vs latency tradeoffs.
2) Redwood Optimize v6 integrations surfaced in Console and API for per-customer quantization suggestions.
3) Dedicated: per-route burst capacity & configurable autoscale cooldowns.
4) Pricing update: new 'Dedicated Reserved Flex' SKU and tiered hosted per-token rates tied to request concurrency bands.
goals_and_okrs:
Primary goals (Q4 2026):
- Reliability: Reduce 99th percentile latency on the Serving tier by 15% for p50-1k token workloads (Owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Cost predictability: Launch pricing tiers and Reserved Flex SKU; target 20% uptake among Dedicated customers in the pilot cohort.
- Developer experience: Add routing policy editor and one-click canary rollouts in Console.
- Observability: Expose token-level cost per route and retention-90-day logs for paid tiers.
OKRs:
1. Decrease customer-reported latency incidents by 30% vs Q3.
2. Achieve GA of model routing UI with 4 pilot customers onboarded.
3. Convert pilot cohort to Reserved Flex signed contracts representing $1.2M ARR incremental.
Owners: Product: Ava Martinez; Eng Runtime: Daniel Kim; Console: Priya Nair; Sales/EM: Marco Alvarez.
requirements:
High-level requirements (PRD):
1) Model routing and fallbacks
   - Must support policy rules evaluating: region, model-cost, latency-SLO, feature-flag.
   - Fallback chain must allow up to 3 fallback variants with percentage-based traffic weights.
   - API: expose 'routing_policy' object (JSON) via CreateRoute and UpdateRoute endpoints.
2) Redwood Optimize integration
   - Console: surface model suggestions and quantization profile per workload sample.
   - API: allow customers to opt-in to ApplySuggestedProfile with 1-click.
3) Dedicated burst capacity controls
   - Per-route burst limit configurable in GPU units.
   - Autoscale cooldown configurable (30s-15m).
4) Pricing & billing
   - Add Reserved Flex SKU with monthly commitment tiers (S/M/L) and overage pricing.
   - Hosted rates: introduce concurrency bands (1-10, 11-50, 51+) with discounts for sustained usage.
5) Observability & SLOs
   - Token-level cost per-request in billing export.
   - 90-day trace retention for Premium customers.
Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests demonstrating fallback correctness with injected failures.
- Billing export shows per-request cost in dev and prod environments.
- Console shows routing policy editor and rollout controls in the UI tests.
Security & compliance:
- All routing configs are logged for audit; changes require RBAC 'route-admin' permission.
- Private deployment: routing policy stored in customer-managed control plane only when confidentiality=restricted is set.
design_spec:
Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Architecture: routing decision happens in the front proxy (edge) for latency-sensitive rules and again in the runtime scheduler for final model selection. This two-stage approach keeps tail latency low while enabling rich policy evaluation.
- Data model: routing_policy is stored as structured JSON in Catalog service. To keep this document flat: example schema described below as text.
Example policy DSL (text):
- rules: [
  - name: 'prefer-low-cost-eu'
    when: region == 'eu' AND expected_tokens < 512
    prefer: ['vicuna-13b-8q', 'redwood-7b-4q']
    fallback_weighting: [70,30]
]
- Implementation details:
  - Cache policy decisions for identical request fingerprints for 60s.
  - Fall back selection uses weighted random with deterministic seed per-request for reproducible A/B comparisons.
- Observability hooks:
  - Emit 'routing.decision' span with fields: chosen_model, policy_id, fallback_chain, decision_time_ms, reason_code.
- Rollout controls:
  - Canary uses traffic-slice by percent and supports automatic rollback if error-rate > threshold for 5m.
Tradeoffs considered:
- Doing full policy evaluation in the control plane simplifies policy authoring but increases latency; chosen hybrid approach reduces p95 impact.
- Using deterministic seeded weighted selection reduces sampling variance for experiments at cost of slightly more complex hashing logic.
Open design questions:
- Should we expose full DSL in API v1 or a limited subset? Recommendation: limited subset for GA and extended DSL in v2.
Owners: Eng Runtime (Daniel Kim), Infrastructure (Liam O'Connor).
roadmap_and_themes:
Roadmap (next 6 months):
- Nov 2026 (GA): model routing cost-aware fallbacks (UI + API), Dedicated per-route burst controls, Redwood Optimize integration v6 (Console + API), Pricing update release.
- Dec 2026: Pilot Reserved Flex contracts with 6 enterprise customers; telemetry-driven tuning of autoscale cooldown heuristics.
- Jan-Feb 2027: Expand routing DSL, add per-customer policy templates, improve offline eval harness for rollout safety.
- Mar-Apr 2027: GA full DSL, add machine-learned routing advisor in Redwood Optimize.
Themes:
1) Production economics: expose levers to trade cost vs latency at config-time and runtime.
2) Safe rollouts: canary + automatic rollback + reproducible sampling.
3) Observability-first: token-level cost, per-route traces, 90-day retention for paid tiers.
Milestones and dependencies:
- Dependency: billing export pipeline needs schema v3 before pricing launch (owner: finance-and-legal).
- Dependency: Console feature flags and RBAC work (owner: eng-platform).
pricing_and_packaging:
Pricing changes (effective 2026-11-20):
- Hosted API:
  - Base: $0.0008 per token for the first 1M tokens / month.
  - Concurrency bands applied as discounts: 1-10 (base), 11-50 (-12%), 51+ (-22%).
  - Premium Support add-on: +$1,000/month (includes 90-day trace retention).
- Dedicated Reserved Flex SKU (new):
  - Small (S): $12,000/month commit, up to 4 GPUs reserved, burst allowance 25% for 30 minutes/day.
  - Medium (M): $40,000/month commit, up to 16 GPUs reserved, burst allowance 50% for 1 hour/day.
  - Large (L): $120,000/month commit, up to 64 GPUs reserved, burst allowance 100% for 2 hours/day.
  - Overage: billed at 1.5x hosted per-token equivalent for bursts above allowance.
- Redwood Optimize integration pricing:
  - Advisory insights (Console) included for all Dedicated customers.
  - Auto-apply quantization profiles: available as an add-on at $0.02/1000 tokens processed for model-reprofiling runs.
Packaging guidance for sales:
- Default GTM for new enterprise customers: suggest Medium Reserved Flex if expected sustained throughput >500k tokens/day.
- For PLG customers: recommend Hosted with concurrency band guidance and Optimize advisory to reduce unit costs.
Billing and implementation notes:
- Billing export schema v3 required. Finance to run a migration plan and ensure backfilled usage for pilot customers.
- Legal to sign amended Dedicated terms covering burst allowances and SLOs.
release_notes:
Release 2026-11-20 (Unified Inference):
Highlights:
- GA: Model routing cost-aware fallbacks (API + Console routing policy editor).
- GA: Dedicated per-route burst capacity controls and configurable autoscale cooldown.
- GA: Redwood Optimize v6 console integrations and 1-click apply for suggested quantization profiles.
- Pricing: Hosted concurrency bands and Dedicated Reserved Flex SKU live.
Fixes and improvements:
- Reduced p99 latency for 512-token workloads by 12% (runtime kernel selection improvements).
- Fixed issue where routing edits were not audited in Private deployments.
- Console: improved UX for rollout percentage sliders and percent-based traffic slices.
Known issues:
- In rare cases (>0.01% of requests) deterministic seeded fallback selection will choose same fallback for correlated request bursts; mitigation scheduled for Dec 2026 patch.
- Reserved Flex billing UI does not yet show burst usage details for the first 48 hours of activation; we will backfill and surface a dashboard in the next release.
How to get the release:
- Hosted customers: changes are live and enabled by default.
- Dedicated customers: contact your Customer Success manager to enable per-route burst controls and Reserved Flex SKUs.
- Private deployments: on-prem bundle available; customers must upgrade control plane to 2026.11.x.
Notes for support and SRE:
- New alert: "routing.decision.latency > 50ms" created under "dashboards-and-alerts/routing".
- Runbook updated: see /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/routing-fallbacks-runbook for triage steps.
rollout_plan:
Rollout plan (GA):
1) Week 0 (canary): Enable feature for internal traffic and 3 pilot customers (10% traffic slice). Monitor error-rate and latency for 72 hours.
2) Week 1: Expand to 25% for pilot cohort, enable billing export schema v3 in staging.
3) Week 2: Gradual ramp to 100% for pilots, open Reserved Flex pilot sales.
4) Week 4: GA for all Hosted customers; default routing policy set to 'prefer-latency' for new routes.
Rollback criteria:
- Error-rate delta > 0.5% over baseline for 10 minutes, OR
- Customer-reported severity-1 incidents related to model selection.
Communication:
- Customer Success: one-pager and email template for customers with Dedicated deployments.
- Docs: update API reference and add routing policy examples.
Owners: Product (Ava Martinez), Eng SRE (Liam O'Connor), Customer Success (Rachel Greene).
metrics_and_slos:
Key metrics to monitor:
- p50/p95/p99 latency for 1-512 token and 512-2048 token buckets.
- Model selection correctness rate (percentage of requests that returned chosen_model vs fallback).
- Billing accuracy: percent of requests with per-request cost present in export (>99.99%).
- Uptake metrics: number of Dedicated customers using Reserved Flex, % of traffic routed via new routing policies.
SLOs for GA:
- Serving latency p95 < 350ms for 1-512 token requests (regional, Hosted).
- Routing decision time p99 < 50ms.
- Billing export delivery success > 99.5% daily.
Alerting thresholds (initial):
- routing.decision.latency > 100ms (P2)
- model-selection.error-rate > 0.3% sustained over 5m (P1)
- billing.export.failures > 0.5% (P1)
